USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Withdrawal risk

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 39-year-old man wants to start bupropion for smoking cessation. He reports daily heavy alcohol intake and plans to stop abruptly that evening without supervision. He has tremulousness when he misses drinks. Which complication is the principal reason to avoid starting bupropion in this setting?

  1. Seizures during alcohol withdrawal
  2. Disulfiram-like acetaldehyde accumulation
  3. Acute opioid withdrawal
  4. Dopamine-blockade dystonia
  5. Irreversible pulmonary fibrosis
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Seizures during alcohol withdrawal

Withdrawal already increases seizure susceptibility; adding bupropion creates an avoidable additional risk.

Understanding the options

Seizures during alcohol withdrawal
Withdrawal already increases seizure susceptibility; adding bupropion creates an avoidable additional risk.
Disulfiram-like acetaldehyde accumulation
Bupropion does not treat alcohol use by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase.
Acute opioid withdrawal
No opioid antagonist is being administered.
Dopamine-blockade dystonia
Bupropion is not a dopamine receptor antagonist.
Irreversible pulmonary fibrosis
This is not the characteristic interaction driving the decision.
